fact: The Communications Authority says its Universal Service Fund financed voice and data infrastructure in 76 sub-locations across 15 counties between 2015 and 2021, giving access to over 500,000 people in unserved areas.

The Communications Authority's USF Strategy 2023-2027 says the Authority will give direct financial support to roll out 2,500 km of fibre in unserved and underserved areas, with a Ksh 40.037 billion plan for the period.
The 2022 KDHS fact sheet gives internet use in the past 12 months, aged 15-49, as 80.0% of urban and 40.7% of rural men and 67.7% of urban and 27.9% of rural women.
The Communications Authority's Director General says the Universal Service Fund has connected nearly 800,000 people in underserved areas, 886 secondary schools, 56 public libraries and 42 law courts.
Kenya News Agency quotes the USF deputy director saying the first three phases of the BTS project covered more than 500 sub-locations, at Sh4 billion.

Principal Secretary Stephen Isaboke says the government continues, through the Universal Service Fund, to support connectivity expansion in underserved areas with mobile coverage gaps, and asks counties to name priority unconnected wards for targeted interventions.

Kenya's Communications Authority says its Universal Service Fund mobile infrastructure phases 1-4 targeted 369 sub-locations and 155 are connected to date, within a KES 17.674 billion, 11-project portfolio with an estimated 1.6 million beneficiaries.

fact: The Communications Authority says its Universal Service Fund mobile project has connected nearly 800,000 people in 171 sub-locations in 24 counties over seven years.

The Communications Authority says its Sh5 billion programme to lay 2,500 km of fibre across 19 counties for rural internet access is 50 per cent complete with 1,300 km laid, and that over five years it deployed base stations across over 130 sub-locations covering over 750,000 people in 24 counties.
